about: The film of the website. The numbers (the length of the film, the start and end of each chapter, the lines) are written by tools/prepare-film.py from the data file the film is made with; do not change them by hand. The rest is the site's own: a chapter begins with the shot fromShot and runs to the next chapter; stillAfter is the moment of its still, in seconds from its start.

film.name: From a wish to a device
film.description: A short film about Teamwright. Somebody wants to build a small sensor hub, a board, its firmware and a case. He tells the Advisor, which proposes a team of AI specialists that run on his own Claude Code, and he manages the work in the program's tracker. The interface in the film is the real program on sample projects; the desk, the person, the board, the parts and the case are modelled for the film.

chapters.title: The wish
chapters.seen: A desk at night under one lamp. A person wants to build a sensor hub, and a notebook holds a pencil sketch of a small box with a screen. A board, firmware and a case are too much for one person. Then the laptop opens on Teamwright.

still.alt: A person sits at a desk at night under one lamp, beside a dark window, a notebook in front of him.

chapters.title: Tell the Advisor
chapters.seen: The real program. The Advisor hears what the manager wants and asks what it needs to know. Then it proposes a team of AI specialists and a plan of tasks, which the manager can change before approving it.

still.alt: The proposal of the Advisor: the project in its words, a team of three specialists with a model and an effort for each, and a plan of fourteen tasks with their owners and what each waits for.

chapters.title: A team on Claude Code
chapters.seen: The team of the project: the manager and three AI specialists, each with its model and effort. Every specialist runs on the Claude Code installed on the manager's own computer, with the manager's own plan.

still.alt: The Team view of a sample project: the manager and three AI specialists, each with what it does, and under them the line that says the specialists run on your own Claude Code, signed in with your plan.

chapters.title: The team at work
chapters.seen: The specialists work on their tasks, hand their results over and write to each other. The office shows who is at work. With the coordinator switched on, ready work starts by itself, within a budget.

still.alt: The office of a sample project: a workshop drawn in plan, with a bench and a person at a desk for every member of the team.

chapters.title: You stay in charge
chapters.seen: A specialist that needs more asks the manager in the inbox, and waits for the answer. When the limit of the Claude plan is reached, the team waits and goes on after. The memory keeps what was decided.

still.alt: The inbox of the manager: a question from a specialist, with the options, what each leads to, and the one it recommends.

chapters.title: Your own team
chapters.seen: Ready-made specialists join the team, each with its own instructions. The team is given skills and connectors, and a connector runs only as the manager confirmed it. The Advisor can start from conversations the manager already had.

still.alt: The Team view with the dialog that adds a ready-made specialist: a list of specialists to choose from, and the instructions of the chosen one, a technical writer.

chapters.title: A full tracker
chapters.seen: The plan lives in a tracker that starts from a template. The board of a sprint, whose lane says when it holds too much; a task with tags, a checklist and fields of its own; the table, where every field is a column; the board grouped by person or by tag.

still.alt: The board of a sample project: tasks in five statuses from To do to Done, each card with its number, what it waits for, its due date, its estimate and who it is given to.

chapters.title: Seeing the work
chapters.seen: The Gantt chart sets the plan against what really happened. Then the sprints with their burndown, the dashboard, a report of the whole project, and the computers the project is kept on.

still.alt: The Gantt chart of a sample project: a bar for every task against the days, with lines from each task to the tasks that wait for it.

chapters.title: Thirteen themes
chapters.seen: One board crossing the thirteen themes of the program, dark and light, three of them new: Rose, Delft and Poppy.

still.alt: The board of a sample project in a light theme of white and blue.

chapters.title: The device
chapters.seen: A schematic draws itself in gold. The board follows, its parts land on it, a small display stands on a header, and the case comes down round it.

still.alt: The finished board of the sensor hub, close up: green, with its parts on it and a small display standing on a header.

chapters.title: Teamwright
chapters.seen: The desk again. A hand pushes in the USB-C cable, the device shows its readings, and the person smiles. Then the name Teamwright, where to find it, and who made it.

still.alt: The finished device on the desk, its cable plugged in and its screen lit, under the name Teamwright.

lines.text: I want to build a sensor hub.
A board. Firmware. A case.
I wish I could.
Teamwright exists.
Tell the Advisor what you want. It asks what it needs to know.
Then it proposes a team of AI specialists, and a plan. Change it before you approve.
Every specialist runs on your own Claude Code, on your computer, with your plan.
They do the work. They hand results over, and write to each other.
Watch the team at work.
Switch the coordinator on, and ready work starts by itself. Within your budget.
When a specialist needs more, it asks you.
When the limit of your plan is reached, the team waits, and goes on after.
What was decided is remembered.
Add ready-made specialists. Give each its own instructions.
Give them skills and connectors. A connector runs only as you confirmed it.
The Advisor can start from conversations you already had.
The plan lives in a full tracker. Start from a template.
Your plan is a board. A lane says when it holds too much.
A task carries tags, a checklist, and fields of your own.
Every field is a column.
Group the board by person, or by tag.
See the plan against what really happened.
Run it in sprints. The burndown follows the scope.
A dashboard that is worked out, not written. And a report of the whole project.
On every computer you own.
Thirteen themes. Three of them new.
Schematic. Layout.
Board, firmware, enclosure. One plan.
You decide. You build it.
You manage. Your team does the work.
You manage. Your team does the work.
